---
title: "Developers"
subtitle: "Get the code, make a change and open a pull request."
---

This page is for you if you want to improve IOSS itself: the sandbox, the game, the scenarios or this website. To play IOSS, read [Get started](get-started.qmd).

## Ways to contribute

You do not have to write code to help.

- **Report a problem or an idea.** Open an [issue](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/issues). Write what you did, what you expected and what happened.
- **Improve a text.** Tour steps, quest tasks, scenario steps and this website are all plain text files.
- **Add a task or a scenario.** Most tasks need only a change in one configuration file.
- **Improve the sandbox.** The setup script and the game master are small Python programs. They use only the standard library.

For a large change, open an issue first. Then we can agree on the design before you write the code.

## Get the code

The practice repository [tinystats](https://github.com/florence-bockting/tinystats) is a Git submodule in `projects/tinystats`. Clone IOSS with its submodule:

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS.git
```

If you already cloned IOSS without the submodule, run this command in the clone:

```bash
git submodule update --init
```

::: {.callout-note}
## No write access?
Fork the repository on GitHub first. Clone your fork. Then add the original repository as `upstream`, so you can get the latest changes:

```bash
git remote add upstream https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS.git
```
:::

## Requirements

| Tool | For |
| :-- | :-- |
| Git | All changes |
| Python 3.11 or later | The sandbox setup and the game master |
| Docker with `docker compose` | The sandbox |
| [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) | This website |

## Project structure

| Folder | Content |
| :-- | :-- |
| `scenarios/` | The scenarios. Each file describes the steps, the roles and the learning goals of one scenario. |
| `seed/` | The planted bugs (`patches/`) and the issue texts (`issues/`) for the practice repository. |
| `projects/tinystats/` | The practice repository, as a Git submodule. |
| `sandbox/` | The local Forgejo instance, its setup script and its CI. |
| `sandbox/tour/` | The guided tour of the repository. |
| `sandbox/game-master/` | The game master, which follows the quest of the player. |
| `site/` | This website. |

## Where to make a change

| You want to change | Edit | Then |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A tour step | `sandbox/tour/assets/steps.js` | Reload the page. |
| A quest task or a reply of an actor | `sandbox/game-master/quests.toml` | Nothing. The game master reads the file for each event. |
| A scenario | `scenarios/*.md` | Nothing. |
| A planted bug or an issue text | `seed/patches/` and `seed/issues/` | Reset the sandbox. |
| The setup of the sandbox | `sandbox/setup.py` or `sandbox/compose.yaml` | Reset the sandbox. |
| This website | `site/*.qmd` | Preview the site. |

::: {.callout-warning}
The seed patches match the commit of tinystats that the submodule points to. If you update the submodule, apply the patches again to make sure that they still work.
:::

The [sandbox README](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/blob/main/sandbox/README.md) and the [seed README](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/blob/main/seed/README.md) explain each part in detail.

## Make a change

1. Update `main`:

   ```bash
   git switch main
   ```

   ```bash
   git pull
   ```

2. Create a branch with a short name that says what you change:

   ```bash
   git switch -c feat/quest-review-task
   ```

3. Make the change. Keep it small: one topic in each branch.

4. Test the change. See [Test your change](#test-your-change).

5. Commit the change:

   ```bash
   git add sandbox/game-master/quests.toml
   ```

   ```bash
   git commit -m "feat: add a quest task for the review"
   ```

6. Push the branch:

   ```bash
   git push -u origin feat/quest-review-task
   ```

7. Open a pull request on GitHub.

### Commit messages

Start each commit message with a type, as in [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

| Type | For |
| :-- | :-- |
| `feat:` | A new function, task or page |
| `fix:` | A bug fix |
| `docs:` | A change to the documentation only |
| `chore:` | Maintenance, for example a submodule update |

## Test your change

Run the unit tests of the game master:

```bash
cd sandbox/game-master && python3 -m unittest
```

Preview the website. Quarto updates the page each time you save a file:

```bash
quarto preview site
```

Test a change to the sandbox in a new sandbox. Run these commands in `sandbox/`.

::: {.callout-warning}
A reset deletes all users, issues and pull requests of the sandbox.
:::

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

```bash
rm .env
```

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

```bash
python3 setup.py
```

Then log in as `newcomer` and play the part that you changed.

## Open a pull request

- **Describe the change.** Write what you changed, why, and how you tested it.
- **Link the issue.** Write `Closes #<number>` in the description. GitHub then closes the issue when the pull request merges.
- **Open a draft** if the work is not finished. Mark it as ready when you want a review.
- **Answer each review comment.** Push a new commit for each requested change.

A maintainer merges the pull request after the review. A change to `site/` goes live on this website a few minutes after the merge.

## Get help

Open an [issue](https://github.com/florence-bockting/IOSS/issues) with your question. A question is a contribution too: it shows us where the documentation is not clear.
